topic: Sylhet mayor's decision to appoint 'unknown' expats as advisors suspended amid criticism
headline_marked: Sylhet BNP [[suspends appointment of 3 'unknown' expats]] as advisors
headline: Sylhet BNP suspends appointment of 3 'unknown' expats as advisors
summary: The decision was reversed after intense criticism and allegations that the appointments violated party constitution and were made without central approval.
details: Sylhet Metropolitan BNP has suspended the decision to include three expatriates—Faisal Ahmed and Mohammad Humayun Milad from the UK, and Saifur Harun from the USA—in its advisory council.
The reversal comes just four days after the appointments were announced on September 13, following widespread criticism from local party members and leaders.
Party members claimed the three individuals were 'unknown' in political circles and had not been active in party activities in their respective countries of residence.
Allegations surfaced that the appointments were made based on the recommendations of an influential minister's brother, bypassing the party's formal constitution.

According to the BNP constitution, the Secretary General must approve the Metropolitan Executive Committee's decisions upon the consultation of the Chairman; local presidents or general secretaries cannot grant such approvals independently.
The issue was raised during an organizational meeting where central leader G K Ghouse expressed anger over the appointments being made without informing the central committee.
Local leaders also questioned how expatriates living abroad could effectively provide advice to party workers and leaders based in Sylhet.
caption:
Three 'unknown' expats were appointed as advisors to Sylhet BNP, but the decision was scrapped within four days after a political firestorm.

Sylhet Metropolitan BNP has suspended the decision to include three expatriates—Faisal Ahmed and Mohammad Humayun Milad from the UK, and Saifur Harun from the USA—in its advisory council.

The reversal comes just four days after the appointments were announced on September 13, following widespread criticism from local party members and leaders.

Party members claimed the three individuals were 'unknown' in political circles and had not been active in party activities in their respective countries of residence.

Allegations surfaced that the appointments were made based on the recommendations of an influential minister's brother, bypassing the party's formal constitution.

According to the BNP constitution, the Secretary General must approve the Metropolitan Executive Committee's decisions upon the consultation of the Chairman; local presidents or general secretaries cannot grant such approvals independently.

The issue was raised during an organizational meeting where central leader G K Ghouse expressed anger over the appointments being made without informing the central committee.

Local leaders also questioned how expatriates living abroad could effectively provide advice to party workers and leaders based in Sylhet.
